title: Opportunistic vs Guaranteed GPU Arbitration with Regional Vendor Affinity and Soft Budget Slices
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We currently lack a unified arbitration layer that treats preemptible (opportunistic) and guaranteed (reserved/on-demand) GPU capacity as two coordinated allocation pools while respecting per-tenant soft budget slices, regional vendor affinity preferences, and model-variant SLO constraints. This ticket defines a runtime-level arbitrator that balances cost and SLOs by classifying requests, applying per-tenant spend windows, preferring vendor/region affinity for model quality, and falling back to degraded model variants or alternate regions when budgets/availability are constrained.

Goals:
- Route requests to the lowest-cost compatible capacity that meets request SLO (latency/throughput) and tenant budget guardrails.
- Provide vendor/region affinity hints so latency-sensitive or HW-optimized models land on preferred instance families when affordable.
- Implement soft budget slices per tenant + per-workload that trigger graceful model-variant or region fallbacks instead of hard rejection.
- Emit telemetry needed for chargeback and debugging (route_decision, budget_state, fallback_reason, latency_estimate).

Out of scope: global rebalancer for long-lived reservations and spot market bidding logic.
acceptance_criteria: Router can classify incoming requests into (opportunistic|guaranteed) candidate sets and make deterministic route decisions in the hot path.
Per-tenant soft budget slices applied; when slice is near-exhaustion router prefers cheaper variants/regions but keeps requests alive with degraded model variants where possible.
Vendor/region affinity honored for flagged models (configurable), with observable fallbacks when affinity is not honored due to budget or capacity.
End-to-end tests demonstrating: P95 latency remains within SLO for prioritized requests, mean cost-per-token reduced for opportunistic-eligible traffic, and fallback counts tracked.
Canary rollout covering <5% traffic with metrics dashboards and automatic rollback on key metric regressions (latency P95 > +15% or fallback rate > 5% of baseline).
design_notes:
High-level design:
1) Decision weights: compute a score for each candidate route = alpha*SLO_score + beta*cost_score + gamma*affinity_score - delta*eviction_risk. Coefficients are tenant-configurable with defaults favoring SLO over cost for high-tier customers.
2) Budget slices: maintain a rolling spend window (e.g., 24h) per tenant and per-route-class. Each request reduces remaining budget; below thresholds router switches to degraded variants or cheaper regions. Slices are soft — they trigger mitigation, not rejection.
3) Candidate generation: enumerate compatible model variants + instance classes (quantized variants, smaller layers, CPU-fallback optionally) across regions. Filter by hard constraints (region locks, compliance).
4) Affinity: store vendor/instance affinity tags per model (e.g., \"A100_fp16\", \"t4-int8\") enforced as a boost in affinity_score.
5) Eviction estimator: track spot eviction history per region/instance class; convert to eviction_risk penalty.
6) Telemetry: emit route_decision event with fields: request_id, chosen_route, candidate_scores, budget_state, fallback_reason, estimated_p95.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs route quality: scoring increases CPU in hot path; we mitigate by caching candidate lists and precomputing coarse scores server-side.
- Soft budgets vs determinism: soft slices may cause increased variability; we use hysteresis windows to avoid flapping.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (core): implement candidate generator, scoring function, and budget slice store (in-memory + persisted checkpoint). Unit tests for scoring and budget arithmetic.
Phase 2 (integration): wire into router hot path with feature flag. Add telemetry events and metrics (chosen_route, fallback_count, budget_exhaustion_rate).
Phase 3 (affinity + eviction risk): add model affinity metadata, eviction history collector, and eviction_risk integration into scoring.
Phase 4 (degraded variants + billing hooks): enable model-variant fallback logic and ensure billing attribution updates with partial-charge semantics in edge cases.
Phase 5 (canary + rollout): deploy to canary, observe metrics, iterate on coefficients and thresholds, schedule full rollout if stable.
rollout_plan: Canary on runtime-1.24: start with 2% tenant traffic across low-risk tenants, monitor latency P50/P95, cost-per-token, fallback_rate, and budget churn. Expand to 10% after 48h if stable. Automatic rollback criteria: latency P95 > +15% baseline or error rate increase > 0.5% absolute. Post-rollout retrospective and tuning session.
metrics: fallback_rate (percent of requests routed to degraded variant)
qa_checklist: Unit tests for scoring logic with synthetic candidates
Integration test that simulates budget depletion and asserts fallback behavior
Load test on canary cluster to validate latency impact < 10% overhead in hot path
E2E billing smoke to ensure spend attribution for mixed-variant requests
